rationale:
Decision unchanged: accept for packaging. All thirteen executed controls passed (reference, empty, recomputed, alternative, missing, plus the eight probes — six wrong-solution, one of them focused on numeric tolerance, and two valid-alternative — every grader run exited 0, every probe executed successfully, every report emitted exactly the four named checks). Counting directly from the supplied records, no control failed or was left unevaluated, so the baseline requirements are met; the balance of this review is what the controls alone cannot establish.

Scope and reference identity. The single approved endpoint (blacklist-filtered peak table with strongest-motif annotation) is the only graded artifact and matches the plan's selected output; excluded notebook branches are not resurrected. The recorded export (sha ffb0b2b6..., 40,557 rows) is projected to the public schema by a positional header rename only, gated on a sha256 check of the export plus a nine-fields-per-line structural check; two materialization replays were byte-identical. The adapted-source oracle's output (sha 97283ee1...) is byte-identical to that projected reference, and the independently written stdlib implementation (sweep-with-heap interval algorithm, executed without answer access, output sha 1c66466e...) passes all four grader checks against it. These two chains are kept distinct and described separately below; no clean-room claim is made about the adapted-source oracle, and the independent run is treated as one cross-implementation data point, not a portability proof.

Contract-to-code tracing. Every clause of the public contract maps to executable behavior: two accepted file locations; UTF-8 with BOM ignored; mixed LF/CRLF with a single optional trailing newline (a second trailing newline is rejected as a blank line, exactly as stated); exact nine-name header tuple; ragged rows, repeated headers, comment lines and header-only tables rejected; per-row typed rules (peak_start >= 0 < peak_end, strictly positive finite peak_fc, nonfinite/underscore-literal rejection in both parsers, all-or-nothing motif block with motif_chrom == peak_chrom, motif_end > motif_start, nonnegative integer motif_pval, strand alphabet {+,-}, and -1/empty sentinel values normalized equal via motif None); two multiplicity-counting multiset comparisons (interval triple, then complete parsed row); alternative integer renderings (+450, 0450, 4.5e2) accepted and genuinely fractional values rejected, matching the contract's own examples. No numeric tolerance exists anywhere, and none is needed: every compared value is copied input text or exact integer interval arithmetic.

Precision/serialization basis. The independent control copies peak_fc verbatim from the input text while the reference renders it through pandas float64 shortest-repr; complete-row multiset equality over all 40,557 rows passes, so both renderings parse to the same value on this dataset — the empirical basis for the no-tolerance rule. The rounding control re-renders 81 of 40,557 fc values to 3 decimals and fails the complete-row comparison with the interval multiset still passing, and the failing side is identified as peak_fc (81 unmatched rows, of which 0 have an fc occurring in the reference for that interval); no other tolerance boundary exists to exercise.

Wrong outputs. Each executed mutation is a well-formed file rejected by parsed-value comparison at the intended named check, not by crash: exported-index column -> output_table_structure; 14 typed-invalid rows (sentinel '0', partially populated motif blocks, negative fc, NaN/inf fc) -> row_values_valid; under-aggressive and over-aggressive trims (chr17 65556624-65556707 extended upstream into padded-blacklist material; chr1 90434472-90434842 shortened by 37 bp) -> retained_peak_intervals and the full-row comparison; merged/dropped/duplicated intervals (3 missing, 2 extra as executed; 40,556 rows) -> interval and full-row comparisons; motif pval/instance/strand/swap changes with an unchanged interval multiset -> peak_fc_and_motif_annotation only; the 81 rounded fc values -> annotation only. Empty and missing submissions fail all four checks. The two valid-alternative probes (row shuffle, integer pval rendering, -1/empty sentinel mixed row by row, trailing-zero fc, dropped trailing newline, outputs/ location, CRLF) pass all four relative checks, confirming the granted equivalences. No probe relies on a crash or a malformed file to carry a substantive branch; the composite retained-set semantics (same-chromosome overlap, earliest-record fc for the 15 duplicate loci, max-pval with earliest-motif-line tie-break, 0-clipped 1 kb union subtraction with 15 loci fully removed and 2 trimmed) are established on the real inputs by the independently executed implementation agreeing with the frozen reference under the grader, cross-validating what table-level controls cannot distinguish (the tie-break and duplicate-loci conventions).

Leakage. The public instruction contains no row counts, hashes or answer values; the grader embeds no result values beyond the contract's constants; check names are not used in any detection logic; failure messages disclose aggregate counts and submission-side rows only; the isolate/empty-submission and internal-error paths convert to failed checks, never to a pass. The candidate's prose claims I checked against the records all matched: 40,557 rows, 5,765 no-motif rows rendered with pval -1.0, pval extent [-1, 1035], fc extent 5.04924-627.60723, strand alphabet {+,-}, 29 chromosome labels.

Non-blocking observations recorded for follow-up, each traced to its grading impact and none an unresolved public-contract mismatch: (1) The motif file's first line is described as a UCSC track-declaration line in the task; the independent solution's rationale prose asserts the staged file begins with a data row (770,050 parsed instances). That assertion is author prose, not controller evidence, and the 770,050 count is consistent with either reading of the first line. Decisive for grading: the instruction, addendum and frozen reference all pin skip-the-first-line, and the executed records show that a solver keeping the first line also passes all four checks against the frozen reference on this data, so no solver following the stated rules can be wrongly failed and no acceptance rule changes; the author's already-planned staged-bytes inspection is a wording fix only. (2) A few value-neutral leniencies are implemented but not exercised by probes (BOM ignore, mixed LF/CRLF, alternative integer renderings, field/header whitespace stripping); verified by inspection, they can only accept additional renderings of the same value and can never wrongly fail a valid submission. (3) Cosmetic: the annotation probe applies 17 edit operations over 16 distinct rows (one chr1 row receives both the pval and swap edits) and the grader correctly reports 16 missing/16 unmatched; the rounding-control message's final clause is slightly contorted in phrasing but its verdict and failing-side identification are correct.

Reviewed against the reviewer instructions with no unresolved issues; the candidate's honesty about the grader's coverage limits (no recomputation at grade time; an error shared by reference and submission out of its reach, carried instead by the recorded oracle and independent executions) is accurate and appropriate.
